methods.steps: Run dot -Tpng input.dot -o diagram.png.
methods.limits: Needs Graphviz installed.

methods.steps: Import pygraphviz as pgv; g = pgv.AGraph("input.dot"); g.draw("diagram.png", format="png", prog="dot").
methods.limits: Draws through Graphviz's layout programs, here dot.

methods.steps: Import pydot; graphs = pydot.graph_from_dot_file("input.dot"); graphs[0].write_png("diagram.png").
methods.limits: Graphviz is installed separately. The example takes the first graph with graphs[0].

methods.steps: File > Open the DST in Inkscape with Ink/Stitch installed. The file opens in Manual Stitch Mode. Then File > Export PNG Image, choose Page, Drawing, Selection or Custom, set the size in pixels, and click Export.
methods.limits: The result is a preview of the stitch paths, not a sewing file.

methods.steps: Import pyembroidery; pattern = pyembroidery.read("input.dst"); pyembroidery.write(pattern, "preview.png").
methods.limits: A library, not a viewer. Embroidery software shows the real stitches and thread colors.

methods.steps: Use the quick-conversion wizard on the GIF to make a cursor.
methods.limits: The page says the editor makes cursors from GIF images.

methods.steps: File > Open the GIF; select the area; Image > Create Static Cursor from Selection; OK in the New Cursor From Image dialog; Draw > Set Cursor Hot Spot, then click the new location.
methods.limits: Reducing the color count can leave jagged borders and dithering.

methods.steps: File > Open imports a GIF as an image; Image > Create Cursor From Image; File > Save As, where cursor images are saved as Windows cursor files.
methods.limits: Pages name no CUR extension in the Save As steps.

methods.steps: Run magick "input.gif[0]" still.tiff.
methods.limits: Index 0 is the first image in the file.

methods.steps: Import Image from PIL; Image.open("input.gif").save("still.tiff"). Call seek on the open image to move to a later frame.
methods.limits: save picks the format from the file extension; seek counts frames from 0.

methods.steps: File > Open the GIF; File > Export As and choose TIFF; pick a compression in the TIFF export dialog.
methods.limits: Compression choices: None, LZW, Pack Bits, Deflate, JPEG.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i input.gif -an output.wmv.
methods.limits: The output format is guessed from the file extension; -an leaves audio out.

methods.steps: In Chrome DevTools open the Device Toolbar, choose More options, then Capture full size screenshot. Run cwebp screenshot.png -o page.webp on the saved image.
methods.limits: cwebp accepts PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP or raw Y'CbCr input.

methods.steps: With a Playwright page showing your document, call page.screenshot(path="page.png", full_page=True). Then use Image.open("page.png").save("page.webp") with Pillow.
methods.limits: Pillow reads and writes WebP; save picks the format from the file extension.

methods.steps: In Chrome DevTools open the Device Toolbar, choose More options, then Capture full size screenshot. Open the screenshot in GIMP, then File > Export As, pick WebP and tick Lossless if you want no quality loss.
methods.limits: The GIMP WebP dialog's Lossless checkbox turns off the quality and alpha quality settings.

methods.steps: Run magick input.jif compatible.jpeg.
methods.limits: Run locally on the sample JIF: it wrote a JPEG of the same pixel size.

methods.steps: From PIL import Image; Image.open("input.jif").save("compatible.jpeg").
methods.limits: Pillow's JPEG quality defaults to 75; the save re-encodes. Run locally on the sample JIF, it wrote a JPEG.

methods.steps: File > Open the JIF; File > Export As, give the file a .jpeg name and click Export; set the JPEG options in the export dialog.
methods.limits: The export dialog offers Quality, Progressive and other options.

methods.steps: Open the JPEG, File > Export, Format > TIFF, then Save.
methods.limits: Preview lists TIFF among its export formats.

methods.steps: Open the photograph; File > Export As, export as TIFF; choose the Compression in the TIFF export dialog.
methods.limits: The dialog offers None, LZW, Pack Bits, Deflate, JPEG and CCITT fax modes; JPEG is lossy.

methods.steps: From PIL import Image; Image.open("input.jpeg").save("delivery.tif", compression="tiff_lzw").
methods.limits: Compression needs libtiff; without it Pillow reads and writes only uncompressed TIFF files.

methods.steps: From PIL import Image; Image.open("input.jpg").save("output.jfif", format="JPEG").
methods.limits: Pillow writes standard and progressive JFIF files. The save re-encodes the pixels.

methods.steps: Run magick input.jpg output.jfif.
methods.limits: The JPEG format is listed as read and write, described as the JFIF format. The pixels are encoded again.

methods.steps: Run djpeg -outfile pixels.ppm input.jpg, then cjpeg -outfile output.jfif pixels.ppm.
methods.limits: djpeg writes PPM by default and cjpeg reads PPM; the JPEG files are in the de facto standard JFIF format. Decoding and encoding again is a new lossy pass.

methods.steps: Run cjxl input.jpg output.jxl.
methods.limits: cjxl compresses JPEG input losslessly by default, so the original JPEG can be rebuilt bit for bit; this page does not do that.

methods.steps: Run magick input.jpg converted.jxl.
methods.limits: Needs the JPEG XL delegate library. This encodes the decoded pixels.

methods.steps: Open the JPG; File > Export As, and save it as a JPEG XL file.
methods.limits: GIMP 2.10.34 added export, limited to 8-bit lossless.

dot.fact: DOT is Graphviz graph text. Node/edge syntax and graph attributes determine layout inputs. Word templates are a distinct extension collision.

dst.fact: Ink/Stitch imports machine formats in Manual Stitch Mode, and its supported format list includes Tajima DST.
Pyembroidery reads DST and writes PNG; default thread-color information requires care.

gif.fact: GIF uses color tables, optional transparent palette indexes and graphic-control timing/disposal information. It does not provide an audio soundtrack.

png.fact: PNG encodes losslessly compressed pixels, with alpha support; media type image/png.

cur.fact: Cursor hotspot identifies the click coordinate; static cursor creation differs from ANI animation.

tiff.fact: TIFF supports multiple image representations and compression variants; TIF is a short extension; media type image/tiff.

wmv.fact: WMV commonly uses Windows Media video within ASF; video/x-ms-wmv is a conventional media label, not a guarantee of codec compatibility.

html.fact: HTML describes document semantics and can refer to separate resource files; WHATWG maintains the Living Standard.
VS Code provides HTML source editing.
Firefox documents opening local files with its platform-specific Open File shortcut.

jpg.fact: JPEG photo encoding usually trades information for compactness and cannot recover lost detail through re-export. JPEG export has no alpha or native editing layers.

jif.fact: Available coordinator-02 formats-F08.json sheet marks JIF as sameAs JPG. Rare suffix input must still contain valid JPEG data; historical JIF layout/date claims omitted.

jfif.fact: JFIF specifies a minimal JPEG interchange structure, including color interpretation and pixel density.
Pillow exposes JFIF marker information and writes standard/progressive JFIF.

jxl.fact: JPEG XL is standardized in ISO/IEC18181 and supports lossless/lossy coding and specialized reversible recompression of JPEG.
The registered JPEG XL media type is image/jxl.

programs.fact: Browser GIF/JPEG support extends to common desktop and mobile browser platforms; a file picker can impose extra suffix restrictions.
Preview documents image conversion and an animated-GIF frame view.
GIMP reads common raster pictures and exports through format-specific dialogs.
